It's ready for you to commit, with the caveats below. While reviewing I found two things and fixed them: the temporary grid-view change was still there, and the touch tests that acceptance criterion 6 requires were missing. Nothing is committed or pushed.

## 1. Automated coverage
I added 12 touch tests to `useWeeklyGridDrag.test.tsx`, alongside the two two-finger tests from earlier:

| Behavior | Test |
|---|---|
| 350ms hold threshold | Nothing is selected at 349ms; selection starts at exactly 350ms |
| 8px movement tolerance | Moving 9px cancels the hold; moving 8px keeps it |
| Quick tap | Toggles one slot, saved exactly once (the hold timer doesn't add a second save) |
| `pointercancel` | One during the hold drops it; one from a different finger leaves the active drag alone |
| Scrolling | `touchmove` is blocked only while a drag is active: not when idle, not during the hold, not after release |
| Context menu | Blocked during a hold; allowed for an idle mouse |
| Mouse vs. touch | Mouse and pen start immediately with no hold (the existing 11 mouse tests also still pass) |
| Hold then drag | Saves on release, deselects when starting on a selected slot, and auto-scrolls at the bottom edge |

To check the tests aren't just passing by luck, I broke the hook in 9 deliberate ways: a 300ms threshold, `>=` in the tolerance check, removing the movement cancel, cancelling the wrong finger, skipping the hold cancel, always blocking scroll, making pen wait, removing tap-to-toggle, and narrowing the context menu block. Each one made a test fail. The hook is back to the real version.

## 2. Acceptance criteria
| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Swipe scrolls, never selects | ✅ Tested, and passed manually (tests 1, 5) |
| 2 | Hold then drag works as in #70, including auto-scroll | ✅ Tested, and passed manually (2–4, 7, 11) |
| 3 | No scrolling under the finger during a drag | ✅ Tested, and passed manually (2) |
| 4 | No context menu, callout or text selection | ✅ Context menu tested and checked manually (8); text selection blocked by `select-none`; the iOS callout fix is in, but no iPhone test yet |
| 5 | Mouse behavior unchanged | ✅ Existing tests unchanged and passing; manual tests 9, 10, 12 passed |
| 6 | Tests for hold threshold, movement cancel, mouse vs. touch | ✅ Done (section 1) |

## 3. Bugs, types and lint
- **Bugs:** none found beyond the two-finger one you caught.
- **Tests:** 253 passed, 4 skipped.
- **TypeScript:** no errors in the changed files. The 89 errors in `packages/features` were already there on main.
- **Biome:** one warning. `noExcessiveLinesPerFunction` flags the hook as over 100 lines; the touch additions pushed it over. Clearing it means splitting the hook, which isn't worth it in this PR, but a reviewer may ask about it.

## 4. Temporary change
It hadn't been reverted, so I ran `git restore` on `schedule-view.tsx`. It's no longer in `git status`.

## 5. Changed files (4 files, +339/−36)
- `hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag.ts`: the long-press hold, cancelling on movement, `pointercancel` matched to the right finger, cancelling on a second contact, the context menu block, and the native `touchmove` scroll block.
- `components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx`: `touch-none` changed to `touch-pan-y` plus `[-webkit-touch-callout:none]`.
- `hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag.test.tsx`: 14 touch tests.
- `components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.test.tsx`: class assertions updated.

**Remaining concerns** (none of these block a commit, but they're worth putting in the PR description):
- Only Windows Chrome touch has been tested. Android Chrome is the biggest unknown, because its own long-press could interrupt the drag. iOS Safari and a stylus with `touch-pan-y` are also untested.
- A second finger landing outside the time slots (on the day headers, say) won't cancel a drag.
- A tap that stops a scroll mid-motion can toggle a cell, because the scroll guard was deliberately left out.

## 6. Ready to commit?
Yes. When you stage, add the four files by name rather than `git add .`, because the untracked `QUIZ-STUDY-NOTES.md` is still in the folder. A suggested title is `feat(schedules): long-press to drag on touch in weekly availability grid`.

There are 25 hook tests and 10 grid component tests, run with Vitest in jsdom. The key point first: they prove the hook's logic, but they can't prove what a real browser does with scrolling. That part was covered by your manual testing.

## `packages/features/schedules/hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag.test.tsx` (25 tests)

**Touch / long press (14 new, for #93)**

| Test | What it shows |
|---|---|
| waits the full long press before a touch starts dragging | Nothing at 349ms; the drag starts at exactly 350ms and follows the finger |
| commits a long-press drag on release | Hold, drag, lift saves the right day and time range |
| deselects when a long-press drag starts on a selected slot | Deselect mode works on touch |
| cancels the hold when the finger moves past the tolerance | Moving 9px means no drag and nothing saved, so swipes scroll instead of selecting |
| keeps the hold when the finger jitters within the tolerance | 8px of finger wobble doesn't cancel the hold |
| toggles a single slot on a quick tap | A tap toggles one slot, saved only once |
| drops the hold when the browser takes over the touch to scroll | `pointercancel` during the hold means no drag |
| ignores pointercancel from a different pointer | A cancel from another finger doesn't end the active drag |
| only blocks touch scrolling while a drag is active | `touchmove` is blocked only during a drag (idle, holding and released all scroll) |
| blocks the context menu during a hold but not for an idle mouse | No long-press menu; right-click still works |
| starts mouse and pen drags immediately without a hold | Mouse and pen don't wait for a hold |
| auto-scrolls during a long-press drag near the bottom edge | Edge auto-scroll works after a hold |
| cancels an active drag without committing when a second finger touches down | Your two-finger bug: the preview reverts, later moves do nothing, nothing is saved |
| never starts a drag when a second finger touches down during the hold | A second finger during the hold blocks the drag |

**Mouse (11 existing, from #70; unchanged and passing)**
These cover:
- preview and save on release
- deselect
- dragging upward
- click to toggle
- staying in the same day's column
- clamping at the end of the day
- cancel reverts the preview
- ignoring right and middle buttons
- read-only mode
- auto-scroll at the bottom edge
- no auto-scroll away from the edges

## `packages/features/schedules/components/WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.test.tsx` (10 tests)
- **Updated for #93:** when editable, cells get `touch-pan-y` and `[-webkit-touch-callout:none]`, and the hour labels don't.
- **Updated for #93:** read-only cells don't get `touch-pan-y`.

## Evidence the tests work
- **They catch real bugs:** I broke the hook in 9 deliberate ways (wrong threshold, wrong tolerance check, cancelling the wrong finger, always blocking scroll, making pen wait, and so on). Each break made a test fail.
- **They caught your bug:** with the old two-finger code put back, the two-finger test failed.
- **Full run:** `TZ=UTC yarn vitest run packages/features/schedules` gives 253 passed and 4 skipped.

## What they can't prove
jsdom doesn't scroll, so these tests can't confirm that a real browser:
- actually scrolls on a swipe
- skips firing `pointercancel` after the hold
- hides the iOS callout

Your 15 manual tests on Windows Chrome cover those. Android, iOS and stylus are still untested.
